title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Directors, Employees and Consultants
tiers.description: All directors, officers, employees, consultants and contractors of CLINUVEL and its related entities; the general population subject to the insider trading prohibition, clearance requirement, close periods, dealing-volume limits and short-term dealing rule.

tiers.name: CEO
tiers.description: The Chief Executive Officer; distinguished only because their own clearance is obtained from the Chair instead of the CEO, and because the CEO (with the Chair) grants clearance, permits exercise of options/rights in prohibited periods, and permits short-term dealing for others.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Members of the Board; distinguished for ASX and Corporations Act notification of dealings, the trustee provisions, and the duty to notify and seek to prohibit dealing by connected persons and investment managers.

tiers.name: Connected persons
tiers.description: A director's spouse, de facto, family members, associated trusts, companies or other third parties contemplating a dealing on the director's behalf (including any company in which such persons hold 20% or more of equity or voting rights), and investment managers acting for the director or a person associated with them.

rules.detail: No standalone derivatives rule. 'Dealing' expressly includes the grant or acceptance of any option or any other present or future, conditional or unconditional right or obligation to acquire or dispose of securities, which sweeps in an OTC put/call; the same clearance and close-period rules then apply.
rules.evidence: the grant to, or acceptance by such person or entity of any option relating to such securities or of any other right or obligation, present or future, conditional or unconditional, to acquire or dispose of such securities

rules.detail: Hedging is not mentioned anywhere in the policy, including in respect of unvested equity incentive securities.

Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar arrangement is an agreement to sell securities and so a dealing requiring the same clearance, and could also engage the short-term dealing rule if within 3 months.
rules.evidence: entry into an agreement to subscribe for, buy or sell, securities

rules.detail: Round-trip 'short and cover' arrangements are expressly named as dealing, so they require the same prior clearance and are also caught by the short-term dealing rule; there is no outright ban specific to short selling.
rules.evidence: arrangements which involve a sale of securities with the intention of repurchasing an equal number of such securities soon afterwards

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named anywhere in the policy.
CFDs are not named; a CFD referencing CLINUVEL securities would fall within the broad 'right or obligation ... to acquire or dispose of' securities and so require clearance.
rules.evidence: the grant to, or acceptance by such person or entity of any option relating to such securities or of any other right or obligation, present or future, conditional or unconditional, to acquire or dispose of such securities

rules.detail: Margin lending is not mentioned anywhere in this policy, despite it otherwise being a detailed and current document.
Granting security, a charge, lien or pledge over CLINUVEL securities is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
Secured financing arrangements of any kind are not mentioned anywhere in the policy.

Buying and selling within a 3-month period, and entering into short-term dealings such as forward contracts, both require prior CEO permission; a short-tenor or forward-like collar would need this separate permission in addition to ordinary clearance.
rules.evidence: directors, employees and consultants may not buy and sell securities within a 3 month period without permission from the CEO. In addition, directors, employees and consultants may not enter into any short term dealings (eg, forward contracts) without permission from the CEO.

clearance.evidence: providing written notice to the CEO in advance so as to obtain such clearance ... The trade may proceed and must be completed within the next seven (7) business days following approval from the CEO or Chair, providing the Company, its directors, employees or consultants are not in possession of price-sensitive information which would prohibit trading.
in the case of the CEO, providing written notice to the Chair in advance so as to obtain such clearance.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: promptly, to enable ASX notification within 5 business days (and Corporations Act substantial-holding notice within 2 business days)
clearance.evidence: The Company has made arrangements with each Director to ensure that the Director promptly discloses to the Company Secretary all the information required by the ASX. ... Directors ... must notify under that Act within 2 business days if they begin to have, or cease to have, a 'substantial holding'.

short_term.basis: buy and sell within a 3 month period; also covers short-term dealings such as forward contracts
short_term.evidence: directors, employees and consultants may not buy and sell securities within a 3 month period without permission from the CEO. In addition, directors, employees and consultants may not enter into any short term dealings (eg, forward contracts) without permission from the CEO.

exceptions.evidence: subscriptions for shares by directors or employees made under an employee share scheme
shares issued under a dividend reinvestment plan or any new issues in which all shareholders are entitled to participate

undertakings or elections to take up entitlements under a rights issue or other offer (including an offer of securities in lieu of a cash dividend); the take up of entitlements under a rights issue or other offer
allowing entitlements to lapse under a rights issue or other offer (including an offer of shares in lieu of a cash dividend)
the sale of sufficient entitlements nil-paid to allow take up of the balance of the entitlements under a rights issue
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer.

severe personal hardship or a pressing financial commitment on the part of the director, employee or consultant that cannot otherwise be satisfied. The determination of whether circumstances are exceptional for this purpose must be made by a majority decision of the board.

the Chair or CEO may allow the exercise of an option or right under an employee share scheme, or the conversion of a convertible security, where the final date for the exercise of such option or right, or conversion of such security, falls during any prohibited period and the director, employee or consultant could not reasonably have been expected to exercise it at an earlier time when they were free to deal.

a dealing in the Company's securities undertaken by that trust will not be regarded as a dealing by the director for the purposes of this policy where the decision to deal is taken by the other trustees acting independently of the director or by investment managers on behalf of the trustees.

exemption_authority: The Board, by majority decision, determines whether 'exceptional circumstances' (eg severe personal hardship or a pressing financial commitment) justify a sale-only exception to a close period; separately, the Chair or CEO may permit exercise of options/rights or conversion of convertible securities falling due in a prohibited period, and may permit short-term dealing (within 3 months) or short-term instruments such as forward contracts, in each case only where not aware of any other reason dealing is prohibited.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Section 3 (The Trading Policy) addresses insider trading, close periods, clearance, dealing-volume limits and short-term dealing but contains no provision on margin loans, secured financing, encumbrance or hedging.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Despite being a comprehensive, recently-adopted (2024) policy, it is entirely silent on collateralising CLINUVEL securities, so the loan leg of a funded collar has no express permission, prohibition or clearance pathway to point to.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A director, employee or consultant may not sell securities exceeding one-third of the average daily trading volume for the last 180 days directly on the market in any one month. ... This limitation does not apply to any off-market transfers or transfers which occur via a "crossing" or similar such transaction.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any on-market unwind or delta-hedging sale by the bank tied to the collar would be constrained by this monthly volume cap, though off-market transfers and crossings are exempt.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors, employees and consultants must not "shop" an excessive number of brokers and/or potential buyers or sellers so that the sale becomes widely known. They must proceed in a discrete manner when buying or selling securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank should limit the number of counterparties or brokers approached when sourcing the hedge or unwinding the position, to avoid breaching this discretion requirement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The trade may proceed and must be completed within the next seven (7) business days following approval from the CEO or Chair, providing the Company, its directors, employees or consultants are not in possession of price-sensitive information which would prohibit trading.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cleared collar must be priced and executed within 7 business days and becomes unexecutable if price-sensitive information arises before signing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A director must ... seek to prohibit any dealing in securities of the Company during a close period ... by or on behalf of any person related to them ... which includes the director's spouse, de facto, family members, associated trusts, companies or other third parties.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar through a family trust or related company does not escape the close-period and clearance regime unless independent trustees, acting without the director's involvement, make the decision.

bespoke_clauses.clause: ASX: CUV | Börse Frankfurt: UR9 | ADR Level 1: CLVLY
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: CLINUVEL also trades via a Frankfurt listing and a US Level 1 ADR programme, but the Policy itself contains no jurisdiction overlay addressing US or German securities law implications of the collar.

summary: CLINUVEL's 2024 policy is comprehensive on dealing generally: its definition catches options and 'any other right or obligation ... to acquire or dispose of' securities, so an OTC put/call is a dealing requiring prior written clearance from the CEO (or, for the CEO, the Chair), executable within 7 business days of approval, outside the two-month close periods before annual/half-yearly results (or one month before quarterly results) and only while free of price-sensitive information. The policy is, however, entirely silent on margin lending, secured financing, encumbrance and hedging - there is no provision addressing a loan secured against the collared shares at all, so the financing leg of a funded collar sits outside the policy's structured controls and its permissibility is untested. Short-term dealing, including 'forward contracts', requires separate CEO permission if within a 3-month period, which would likely capture a short-tenor collar. Any unwind sale is also constrained by the on-market volume cap (one-third of 180-day average daily volume per month) and a requirement not to 'shop' the trade around brokers, though off-market and private transactions to sophisticated investors are permitted more freely. Overall, the equity/derivative legs of a funded collar look achievable under CEO/Chair clearance and timing rules, but the loan/security leg is simply unaddressed by this policy, so the bank cannot point to any express permission or prohibition for the pledge itself.
